Nova is interested in a short pilot to validate on their prompt set with VPC/private run; security docs and pricing requested.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-10 15:00 PST | Duration: 42m | Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Maya (Nova Head of ML), Liam (Infra), Priya (CTO)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, I'm Jordan, AE on the Redwood team, and Samir is our solutions engineer who will run through the Optimize quant walkthrough. how are we doing, maya?

[00:18] Maya: good, thanks, yes we got the invite. excited to see the int8/fp8 stuff - we've been seeing big token costs on chat.

[00:25] Samir: awesome. i'll share my screen, you might see a slight delay, um, but i'm going to walk through the Optimize UI and then dive into the quantization profiles, show some perf numbers and quality deltas.

[00:40] [screen share starts - UI shown] Samir: ok, this is the Optimize tab. you'll notice we surface recommended profiles by workload - chat, system prompts, long form - and we provide simulated quality vs latency curves. so for Nova, typical chat workloads often pick INT8_profile_A or FP8_profile_B depending on quality tolerance.

[01:12] Liam: quick q - are these recommendations automated via your agents or do they come from manual runs?

[01:20] Samir: good call. Optimize uses an automated profiling job that runs a candidate set of quantizations on a sample of your prompt set - it's heuristics + supervised validation. we run latency microbenchmarks, compute token throughput, and then run your quality evals against the reference responses. so it's semi-auto; you can tune the thresholds.

[01:48] Jordan: to add - we also have a canary rollout in the Console, so you can push INT8 to a small percent of traffic, monitor quality regressions, and roll back automatically if metrics drop.

[02:05] Priya: the security bit is important for us. we run in a VPC and all KMS keys are customer-managed. do you support KMS/HSM and SOC2 baseline?

[02:16] Samir: yes, we support customer KMS, HSM integration for private deployments, and our hosted API is SOC 2 Type II. i'll share the security pack after the call. (note: transcription missed 'HSM' once earlier in docs)

[02:35] Maya: thanks. can you show the actual latency/quality numbers? we've seen claims of 2x latency improvement with int8 but quality drop is a big unknown.

[02:46] Samir: absolutely. here's a short table from our Optimize bench. baseline is FP16 (default). INT8_profile_A: ~30-45% latency reduction at tail percentiles, throughput up 1.8x, quality delta approx -0.8% BLEU-ish metric on the sampled set. FP8_profile_B: latency reduction ~20-30%, throughput up 1.4x, quality delta around -0.3%. these numbers vary by model and prompt distribution.

[03:30] Maya: ok that aligns with what we expected. is FP8 generally safer for hallucination-sensitive tasks?

[03:38] Samir: yes, FP8 tends to preserve numerical fidelity better, so for hallucination/precision-sensitive prompts we recommend FP8 or mixed profiles. INT8 is great for high throughput low-criticality tasks like bulk reranking or embeddings.

[04:02] Liam: what's the incremental complexity to deploy INT8 or FP8 on Dedicated or Private deployments?

[04:09] Jordan: from a config perspective, you pick a quant profile in the deployment template. for Redwood Dedicated we push the optimized kernels automatically; for Private you run a short compile step we orchestrate. Samir can detail the compile step.

[04:24] Samir: compile is usually a few minutes per model variant - we select kernels optimized for your GPU generation. on A100 it's faster, on older cards up to 10-15 mins. the runtime will also do KV cache optimizations - apologies if 'KV cash' shows up in logs, that's a transcriber quirk - but KV cache is preserved across quant levels.

[05:00] Maya: any change to tokenization or output formatting to be aware of?

[05:05] Samir: no, tokenization is identical; only the model weights are quantized. occasionally you see minor probability shifts which manifest as small wording changes; that's the quality delta.

[05:28] [06:00] Samir: demo time - i'm going to run a live generate: same prompt under three profiles: FP16 baseline, FP8_profile_B, INT8_profile_A. watch the latency and output side-by-side.

[06:15] [live demo audio; keyboard noises] Samir: FP16 took 420ms p50, FP8 330ms p50, INT8 240ms p50 on this small seq length. output differences - FP16: "...recommended approach is to validate..."; FP8: "...recommended approach is validate..." minor wording; INT8: one extra sentence trimmed, slightly more terse.

[07:05] Maya: the outputs look fine, but our success criteria are more around intent preservation on 200 prompts.

[07:14] Samir: understood. Optimize lets you upload your prompt set and define an eval - rouge/bleu/embedding-similarity or custom heuristics - and it'll score each profile, produce a quality curve, and let you set a policy threshold for automatic rollouts.

[07:35] Liam: about rollouts - if we see a regression, how fast is rollback and is there any state to worry about?

[07:44] Jordan: rollbacks are immediate server-side routing changes; no model state is lost. KV caches might be cold briefly but we have sticky routing options to preserve caches for canary traffic.

[08:05] Priya: what's a typical delta in hallucination rate you've seen when moving to INT8?

[08:12] Samir: it depends. for chat generative tasks we typically see 0.5-1.5% increase in some hallucination metric for INT8 profiles vs FP16; for FP8 it's usually <0.5%. again depends on model and prompts.

[08:40] Maya: will Optimize show per-prompt failure cases?

[08:45] Samir: yes, it will flag prompts where similarity falls below the threshold and show diffs, so you can inspect which prompts fail and why.

[09:05] [09:30] Jordan: price question - INT8/FP8 profiles affect unit economics because less GPU time, so cost per token drops. i'll send a pricing sheet but ballpark is 20-40% cost reduction for FP8, 35-60% for INT8 depending on throughput and model.

[09:50] Maya: good. one more compliance ask - do you keep audit logs for inference requests and do you support SAML/SSO for Console?

[09:58] Samir: yes, audit logs are available for Private and Dedicated, and hosted has an audit retention add-on. SAML/SSO and RBAC are supported on the Console. we'll include screenshots in the security pack.

[10:20] Priya: for the pilot, we want to test in our VPC with customer-managed KMS. what's the easiest path?

[10:29] Jordan: two options: Redwood Private on your infra (full control) or Dedicated with VPC peering and customer KMS. for speed, Dedicated peering is quickest; Private is more involved but gives full control.

[10:45] Liam: we prefer Dedicated peering for a first pass. we'll do peering and a small test fleet.

[11:00] Samir: perfect. for the bench we'll need the prompt set, sequence length distribution, and an expected qps target. we'll run FP16/FP8/INT8 and return csv with latency histograms, token throughput, and per-prompt quality deltas.

[11:25] [12:00] Maya: can we talk about model variants - what if you need to fallback to a safer variant?

[12:08] Samir: we support routing rules. Optimize can define fallback policies: if quality drops beyond X or latency spikes, route to a safer FP16 variant or alternate region. these are configurable per-route.

[12:32] Maya: what's the expected time to onboard new models into Optimize?

[12:38] Samir: depending on size, a couple hours to profile and generate candidate quant profiles; bigger models take longer. once profiles are generated you can run the eval in a few minutes.

[13:05] Jordan: ok quick recap - Nova will share the 200-prompt set, Jordan will send pricing and security docs, Samir will run a bench and return results, Liam will provision peering. target dates listed in next steps.

[13:25] Priya: one last thing - any proprietary IP or extraction risks with quantized weights?

[13:32] Samir: quantization is a transformation of weights; we don't expose raw weights. for Private deployments you control the model artifacts. we'll include the IP/terms note in the security pack.

[14:00] [14:45] Maya: ok that sounds good. thanks for the demo. any other questions?

[14:50] Jordan: not from us. we'll follow up with the packet. thanks everyone.

[15:05] [call ends, small offline chatter]

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings (HSM spelled out once), some timestamps reflect screen-share moments. latency numbers are approximate from demo environment and will vary on Nova hardware.
